title: Why Menelaus is not a relabelling of Ceva
content: Ceva (concurrent cevians) and Menelaus (a collinear transversal) share the *same unsigned* product relation $\sin_\kappa(BD)\,\sin_\kappa(CE)\,\sin_\kappa(AF) = \sin_\kappa(DC)\,\sin_\kappa(EA)\,\sin_\kappa(FB)$. What distinguishes them is the **parity of external divisions**: a transversal meets the three extended sides in an *odd* number of external points, so its *signed* ratio product is $-1$, whereas concurrent cevians give $+1$. Faithfully formalising Menelaus therefore means working with signed ratios and the value $-1$ — a genuinely different algebraic statement from the parent's $+1$ law, not a rename. Copying `ceva_unified_principle` verbatim with $=1$ would have been the rename; this file deliberately states $=-1$.
mathContext: Same unsigned law; signed value $+1$ (Ceva, concurrence) vs $-1$ (Menelaus, collinearity).

title: Building on the parent and grandparent entries
content: The file imports the grandparent `Proofs.CevasTheoremNonEuclidean` (which supplies the curvature-free `ceva_unified_principle` for an arbitrary positive ratio function $\rho$) and the parent `Proofs.CevasTheoremNonEuclideanOQ01` (which defines the curvature sine `sinKappa` and the curvature-$\kappa$ Ceva theorem `kappa_ceva`). Opening `CevasNonEuclideanOQ01` makes `sinKappa` and its specialization lemmas `sinKappa_one`/`sinKappa_neg_one`/`sinKappa_zero` directly available. No CRT-style construction is rebuilt; this entry only adds the dual signed Menelaus layer.
mathContext: Reuses `sinKappa κ` and `ceva_unified_principle ρ` from the ancestor entries.

title: The sign-distinguished unified Menelaus principle
content: `menelaus_unified_principle` states, for an abstract positive ratio function $\rho$, that the signed product $\bigl(-\tfrac{\rho(BD)}{\rho(DC)}\bigr)\cdot\tfrac{\rho(CE)}{\rho(EA)}\cdot\tfrac{\rho(AF)}{\rho(FB)} = -1$ iff the unsigned cross-multiplied relation holds. The proof is a two-step reduction to the grandparent's `ceva_unified_principle`: a single `ring` rewrite pulls the transversal sign out front, turning the left side into $-X$ where $X$ is the Ceva product; then `neg_inj` collapses $-X = -1$ to $X = 1$, exactly the hypothesis of the unsigned principle. The sign is thus *orthogonal* to all the geometric content — it is factored away before any curvature appears.
mathContext: $-X = -1 \iff X = 1$ (via `neg_inj`), reducing the signed Menelaus law to the unsigned `ceva_unified_principle`.

title: The unified curvature-κ Menelaus theorem
content: `kappa_menelaus` instantiates the abstract principle at $\rho = \sin_\kappa$, yielding a single collinearity criterion valid at *every* curvature $\kappa$ — the Menelaus counterpart of the parent's `kappa_ceva`. There is no new proof work: the body is literally `menelaus_unified_principle (sinKappa κ) …`. All the geometry is encoded in the curvature sine and all the configuration data in the sign, so one statement covers spherical, hyperbolic, and Euclidean geometry at once.
mathContext: $\rho := \sin_\kappa$ specializes the abstract principle to a curvature-parametrised Menelaus law.

title: Recovering the three classical Menelaus laws
content: The three classical theorems fall out as the cases $\kappa = 1, -1, 0$. `kappa_menelaus_spherical` rewrites $\sin_\kappa$ to the ordinary sine via `sinKappa_one`, `kappa_menelaus_hyperbolic` to $\sinh$ via `sinKappa_neg_one`, and `kappa_menelaus_euclidean` to plain segment lengths via `sinKappa_zero`. Each proof instantiates `kappa_menelaus` at the relevant curvature, `simp only`s with the specialization lemma, and applies the positivity hypotheses. The key structural fact (inherited from the parent's Ceva work) is that the $\sqrt{|\kappa|}$ normalization inside $\sin_\kappa$ cancels within every ratio, so the criterion has identical *shape* across all three geometries — only the function applied to the arc lengths changes.
mathContext: $\kappa = 1 \to \sin$, $\kappa = -1 \to \sinh$, $\kappa = 0 \to$ length; the $\sqrt{|\kappa|}$ factor cancels in each ratio.

title: The Ceva–Menelaus duality and mutual exclusivity
content: `ceva_menelaus_duality` is the pointwise algebraic identity that the signed Menelaus product of three feet is literally the negative of their signed Ceva product — proved by `ring` alone, valid at every curvature and for all arguments. `ceva_menelaus_exclusive` then substitutes the Ceva concurrence value $1$ into the duality: feet satisfying $\text{(signed Ceva)} = 1$ automatically satisfy $\text{(signed Menelaus)} = -1$. Since $1 \neq -1$, no configuration can satisfy both criteria with the same value — concurrence and collinearity are mutually exclusive. This is the structural reason the two classical theorems share *one* unsigned product law yet describe opposite configurations.
mathContext: $\bigl(-\tfrac{a}{b}\bigr)\tfrac{c}{d}\tfrac{e}{f} = -\bigl(\tfrac{a}{b}\tfrac{c}{d}\tfrac{e}{f}\bigr)$; substituting the Ceva value $1$ gives the Menelaus value $-1$.
